source_group: Quantitative and academic evidence; anomaly-based swing strategies; systematic tests of technical rules

grade_rubric.A: Replicated out of sample and internationally; survives value-weighting / NYSE breakpoints and realistic costs; persists after publication
grade_rubric.B: Robust and replicated but weaker after publication, cost-sensitive, or with limited post-2015 verification
grade_rubric.C: Weak or mixed: fails VW or large-cap tests, gross-only, microcap-driven, or decayed to marginal
grade_rubric.D: No demonstrated net edge (practitioner backtest only, failed data-snooping tests, or descriptive statistics)

method_notes: Numbers were read from primary PDFs (Daniel-Moskowitz, Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen, Barroso thesis, Cederburg et al., Hou-Xue-Zhang NBER w23394, Martineau, Da-Gurun-Warachka, Lo-Mamaysky-Wang) where possible, otherwise from abstracts or reputable summaries. Items citing the 'prior sweep' reuse figures fact-checked in docs/research-raw/methods-sweeps/evidence.json and docs/methods-factcheck.md. HXZ figures are from the NBER working-paper version (447 anomalies, sample through 2014). The published RFS version reports 452 anomalies and 65%.
corrections_to_prior_sweep: Park-Irwin 2007 (J. Econ. Surveys) reports 95 studies: 56 positive / 20 negative / 19 mixed. The prior sweep's 92 / 58 / 24 / 10 are the 2004 AgMAS report figures.

52-week-high momentum is significant only at the 6-month horizon in value-weighted / NYSE-breakpoint replication (HXZ: 0.57%/mo, t=2.02) and insignificant at 1 and 12 months. Grade it C, not as a top-tier edge.

items.name: Cross-sectional momentum 12-1 (winners minus losers, UMD/WML)
items.brand_or_source: Jegadeesh-Titman (JF 1993); Fama-French UMD; Daniel-Moskowitz (JFE 2016) WML definition
items.rules_or_formula: Each month-end t: universe = common stocks with a valid price and at least 8 of the past 11 monthly returns (DM filter). Signal = cumulative return from month t-12 to t-2, i.e. skip the most recent month t-1 (the skip avoids the 1-month reversal). Sort into deciles using NYSE-only breakpoints (prevents microcaps from filling the extreme deciles). Long the top decile (optionally short the bottom), value-weight, hold 1 month, rebalance monthly. A K-month holding variant runs K overlapping cohorts and averages them. Daily-data proxy: adjClose[t-21]/adjClose[t-252]-1.
items.data_needed: Adjusted daily or monthly closes; shares outstanding for market cap (VW weights and NYSE breakpoints); ideally a survivorship-free universe that includes delisted names
items.evidence: JT 1993: about 1%/month for 1965-89. Hou-Xue-Zhang replication (VW, NYSE breakpoints, through 2014): R11 1-month hold 1.19%/mo (t=4.06), 6-month hold 0.81% (t=3.14). DM 2016, 1927-2013: WML Sharpe 0.71, winners +15.3%/yr excess and losers -2.5%/yr, CAPM alpha 22.3%/yr. Crashes: in Jul-Aug 1932 losers rose 232% against winners' 32%. In Mar-May 2009 losers rose 163% against winners' 8%. In bear markets WML's up-market beta (-1.51) is about twice its down-market beta (-0.70). Prior sweep (Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz live costs): implementable after costs. Jensen-Kelly-Pedersen 2023: momentum replicates globally.
items.holding_period: Rank monthly; hold 1-12 months. For swing trading it is a universe/ranking filter, not a trade trigger
items.post_publication_and_costs: McLean-Pontiff: average anomaly -58% after publication. Momentum survives but is weaker and crash-prone. Turnover is high, so a buy/hold spread (enter top 10%, exit only below the top 20-30%) cuts costs (Novy-Marx-Velikov).
items.swing_engine_use: Primary relative-strength rank for the candidate list. Combine with E04, E05 and E13/E14 crash control.

items.name: Jegadeesh-Titman 6-1 momentum (J=6, K=6, skip a week or month)
items.rules_or_formula: Each month: rank stocks on the past 6-month return (HXZ uses months t-7..t-2, skipping t-1; JT skipped 1 week). Long the top decile, short the bottom. Hold K=6 months with 6 overlapping cohorts, each cohort carrying 1/6 weight. JT equal-weighted with all-stock breakpoints.
items.evidence: JT 1993 (1965-89): about 12% annualized, roughly 0.95%/month for 6/6 with a one-week skip (secondary summary). HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): R6 1-month hold 0.60% (t=2.04), 6-month 0.82% (t=3.49), 12-month 0.55% (t=2.90), against JT's 1.1% (t=3.61) and 0.9%. q-factor alphas -0.04/0.24/0.16 are insignificant.
items.post_publication_and_costs: About 25-50% smaller in VW/NYSE-breakpoint replication than JT's original numbers.
items.swing_engine_use: Shorter-lookback relative-strength rank. Use a 126-trading-day lookback skipping 5-21 days on daily data.

items.name: Industry momentum
items.rules_or_formula: HXZ implementation: use the Fama-French 49 industries, dropping financials to leave 45. Each month sort industries on their prior 6-month value-weighted return over t-6..t-1 (no skip month, following MG). Form 9 portfolios of 5 industries each, equal-weighted across industries. Long the top portfolio, short the bottom. Hold 1, 6 or 12 months. MG: predictability is strongest at the 1-month horizon and lasts up to a year, and industry momentum explains much of stock momentum.
items.data_needed: Industry codes (SIC from SEC EDGAR, free) plus stock returns, or sector/industry ETFs as a proxy
items.evidence: HXZ (VW): Im1 0.67%/mo (t=2.74), Im6 0.60% (t=3.08), Im12 0.64% (t=3.71). MG 1999: highly profitable after controlling for size, B/M, stock momentum and microstructure.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Survives replication. No skip month is needed because industry portfolios do not show 1-month reversal.
items.swing_engine_use: Sector-strength overlay: prefer swing longs in the top-ranked industries or sector ETFs.

items.name: Residual (idiosyncratic) momentum
items.rules_or_formula: Each month: regress each stock's excess returns on the Fama-French 3 factors over the prior 36 months (all 36 required) to get residuals e. Score = sum (or mean) of e over t-12..t-2 divided by the standard deviation of e over the same window. Deciles; long the top decile (short the bottom). Hold 1 month. HXZ also tests a 6-month version (t-7..t-2).
items.data_needed: Monthly returns plus Fama-French factors (free from the Ken French Data Library)
items.evidence: BHM: risk-adjusted profits about twice those of total-return momentum. More consistent over time and less concentrated in the extremes, because time-varying factor exposures are stripped out. HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): 11-month residual momentum 1-month hold 0.67% (t=3.91), 6-month 0.55% (t=3.94), 12-month 0.36% (t=2.96). 6-month residual 6/12-month holds 0.49% (t=3.86) and 0.39% (t=3.92). The 6-month residual with a 1-month hold (0.20%) is insignificant.
items.post_publication_and_costs: HXZ t-stats are higher than for raw momentum, so it holds up better in VW tests.
items.swing_engine_use: Prefer the residual-momentum rank over the raw 12-1 rank to avoid buying pure beta or sector bets after rebounds.

items.name: Frog-in-the-pan (information discreteness) momentum filter
items.rules_or_formula: ID = sgn(PRET) x (%neg - %pos). PRET = cumulative return over months t-12..t-2. %pos and %neg = share of trading days in that window with positive and negative returns. Variant: ID_Z = sgn(PRET)(%neg-%pos)/(%neg+%pos). Procedure: $5 price filter, sort into quintiles on PRET, then into ID sub-portfolios. Buy winners with the lowest ID (continuous, many small up-days). Hold 6 months.
items.evidence: 1927-2007: 6-month momentum rises monotonically from -2.07% (discrete-information winners) to 5.94% (continuous). With independent double-sorts it rises from -0.63% to 5.72%. Continuous-information momentum lasts about 8 months; discrete-information momentum is insignificant after 2 months. No long-run reversal.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Only partly verified out of sample in this pass (Alpha Architect uses it live in its momentum process).
items.swing_engine_use: Quality-of-trend filter. Among relative-strength leaders, prefer smooth grinders over gap-driven spikes.

items.name: 52-week-high proximity momentum
items.rules_or_formula: PTH = month-end price at t-1 / highest split-adjusted daily price over the 12 months ending at t-1 (HXZ definition). GH rank on PTH, buy the stocks nearest their 52-week high and short the farthest, over a 6-month holding period. HXZ: deciles; because many stocks sit exactly at PTH=1, breakpoints use only PTH<1.
items.evidence: GH 2004: nearness to the 52-week high dominates past individual and industry returns as a predictor, and its forecasts do not reverse long-run (anchoring). HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): 6-month hold 0.57%/mo (t=2.02, q-alpha -0.01). 1-month hold 0.14% (t=0.43) and 12-month 0.45% (t=1.88) are insignificant. Prior sweep: international profits in 17 of 18 markets.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Strong in equal-weighted original tests, weak in value-weighted replication. The exact GH 30%/30% cutoffs and spreads were not re-verified here.
items.swing_engine_use: Feature, not a standalone signal. Use near-high (PTH>0.9) as a breakout-context filter alongside 12-1 momentum.

items.name: Short-term (1-month) reversal
items.rules_or_formula: Each month: rank on the month t-1 return (about 21 trading days). Long the bottom decile (losers), short the top (winners). Hold 1 month. Cost-aware version (de Groot et al.): large caps only, weekly rebalance, and a turnover-limiting construction.
items.evidence: Jegadeesh 1990: -1.99%/mo (t=-12.55), equal-weighted with all-stock breakpoints (as quoted by HXZ). HXZ VW NYSE: -0.26% (t=-1.31), failing replication. de Groot-Huij-Zhou: limiting to large caps leaves 30-50 bp/week net of costs. Medhat-Schmeling 2022: reversal lives in low-turnover stocks, while high-turnover stocks show continuation (E09). Dimensional (prior sweep): impractical standalone; useful as an entry-timing overlay.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Mostly a microcap / bid-ask-bounce effect in EW tests. Turnover near 100%/month makes costs the binding constraint.
items.swing_engine_use: Entry timing: within long-momentum candidates, buy after a 1-4 week pullback, but only in low-turnover names and not after an earnings or news gap.

items.name: Weekly / daily contrarian reversal
items.rules_or_formula: Lehmann: buy last week's losers and sell last week's winners, rebalancing weekly. Lo-MacKinlay-style daily version (as used by Khandani-Lo): weights proportional to the negative of each stock's prior-day return minus the cross-sectional mean return, giving a dollar-neutral book (exact scaling not re-verified).
items.evidence: Lehmann 1990: weekly winners and losers reverse sharply the next week. Contrarian profits exceeded 2%/month and persisted after bid-ask and plausible costs (abstract, 1960s-80s). Khandani-Lo: the simple daily contrarian's profitability fell steadily from 1995 to 2007 (secondary summary: gross annualized Sharpe about 53.9 in 1995 vs 2.8 in 2007) as market-neutral capital grew. It then crashed in the August 2007 quant unwind.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Arbitraged by stat-arb funds. The gross Sharpe figures are pre-cost artifacts of daily rebalancing.
items.swing_engine_use: Do not run standalone. At most a tie-breaker for entry day selection.

items.name: Short-term momentum in high-turnover stocks
items.rules_or_formula: Monthly double sort on the prior-month return (t-1) and prior-month share turnover (volume / shares outstanding). In the highest-turnover decile, go long prior-month winners and short losers (short-term momentum). Low-turnover stocks show the classic reversal. NYSE-AMEX-Nasdaq non-financials 1963-2018, value-weighted, monthly rebalance.
items.data_needed: Daily volume and closes, plus shares outstanding (SEC filings / Alpha Vantage OVERVIEW)
items.evidence: As profitable and persistent as conventional momentum. Survives transaction costs. Strongest among the largest, most liquid and most covered stocks (abstract and summaries). Exact decile spreads were not fetched in this pass.
items.post_publication_and_costs: One 2022 paper, so little post-publication evidence yet. Sort details (conditional vs independent deciles) are not verified.
items.swing_engine_use: Swing-relevant: a big 1-month move on high relative turnover in a large cap is a continuation candidate, not a fade. Gate E07 reversal entries on turnover.

items.name: Time-series momentum (trend following)
items.rules_or_formula: Per instrument, monthly: r_TSMOM(t+1) = sign(r[t-12,t]) x (40% / sigma_(t-1)) x r(t+1). Ex-ante variance sigma^2 = 261 x sum_i (1-d) d^i (r_(t-1-i) - rbar)^2 with d set so the center of mass d/(1-d) = 60 days. Average across instruments. HOP: 1-, 3- and 12-month lookbacks, portfolio scaled to 10% ex-ante volatility, 67 markets 1880-2016.
items.data_needed: Daily closes of liquid futures or ETFs (indexes, bonds, commodities, FX)
items.evidence: MOP: 12-month TSMOM is positive for all 58 futures and significant for 52 (1985-2009). Out of sample 1966-85 Sharpe is 1.1, with large gains in extreme markets (the 'smile', Oct-Dec 2008). HOP: positive every decade since 1880, net Sharpe about 0.4 after 2/20 fees (secondary). Critiques: Huang-Li-Wang-Zhou (JFE 2020) find asset-by-asset predictability weak, pooled t-stats below bootstrap critical values, and profits close to a sample-mean strategy's. Kim-Tse-Wald (2016): alpha 1.27%/mo with vol scaling vs 0.41% without.
items.post_publication_and_costs: The live CTA record is weaker than backtests (prior sweep: SG Trend about 5.3% CAGR). Much of the benefit is vol-scaling and diversification.
items.swing_engine_use: Market/sector regime: allow swing longs in an asset only when its 12-month (and 3-month) excess return is positive. Size positions by inverse EWMA volatility.

items.name: Trend filter: 10-month SMA / 200-day
items.rules_or_formula: At each month-end: hold the asset if its month-end close is above the 10-month SMA of month-end closes, else move to T-bills. GTAA applies this to 5 equal-weight asset classes, rebalanced monthly, ignoring costs and taxes. The daily analog is close vs SMA(200).
items.evidence: Faber (data from 1901): equity-like returns with much lower volatility and drawdowns. Zakamulin (prior sweep, 150+ years, out-of-sample windows): higher Sharpe comes mainly from sitting in cash about a third of the time. No statistically significant outperformance in the later half of the sample; it whipsaws in choppy bull markets.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Rated B as a drawdown reducer, C as a return enhancer.
items.swing_engine_use: Index-level gate. Cut gross exposure or new long entries when SPY or the sector ETF is below its 10-month or 200-day SMA.

items.name: Volatility-managed portfolios (inverse lagged variance)
items.rules_or_formula: f_sigma(t) = (c* / sigma^2_(t-1)) x f(t). sigma^2_(t-1) = realized variance of the strategy's daily returns in the previous month. c* is a constant giving the managed series the same full-sample variance as the original.
items.evidence: MM 2017: positive alphas in spanning regressions for the market and many factors. COWY 2020 (103 equity strategies): no systematic Sharpe improvement in direct comparisons. Real-time out-of-sample combinations earn lower Sharpe and CER than unmanaged portfolios, because the spanning regressions are structurally unstable.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Benefits are concentrated in momentum (E13) and are fragile elsewhere.
items.swing_engine_use: Use vol targeting for risk control (keep portfolio risk stable), not as an alpha source.

items.name: Constant-volatility (risk-managed) momentum
items.rules_or_formula: Variance forecast: sigma^2_t = 21 x sum over j=0..125 of r^2_(WML,d-j) / 126 (126 daily returns, about 6 months). Scaled WML = (sigma_target / sigma_t) x WML with sigma_target = 12% annualized. 1-month and 3-month realized variance and EWMA half-lives of 1, 3 and 6 months gave nearly identical results.
items.data_needed: Daily returns of the momentum portfolio
items.evidence: US 1927-2011: Sharpe 0.53 to 0.97, excess kurtosis 18.24 to 2.68, skew -2.47 to -0.42. Plain momentum's worst month was -78.96%. The scaled strategy compounds to about 90x the plain one.
items.post_publication_and_costs: COWY 2020 caution applies, though momentum is the best-case factor for vol management.
items.swing_engine_use: Scale the whole momentum/breakout book by 12% / trailing 126-day realized vol of a long-short momentum proxy, or of the book itself.

items.name: Momentum crash regime filter / dynamic momentum
items.rules_or_formula: Bear indicator I_B = 1 if the cumulative market return over the past 24 months is negative. In bear states WML behaves like a short call on the market (up-beta -1.51 vs down-beta -0.70). Dynamic weight w* = (1/(2*lambda)) x mu_t / sigma^2_t. mu_t comes from a regression of WML on I_B x market variance over the prior 126 days (bear-state intercept shift -2.04%/mo, t=-3.4). sigma_t blends a GJR-GARCH forecast with the 126-day realized std of WML.
items.evidence: The dynamic strategy more than doubles static WML's Sharpe and alpha. Across markets and asset classes the combined dynamic Sharpe is 1.18, four times static US equity momentum's. Caveat: GARCH and regression parameters are fit on the full sample.
items.swing_engine_use: Swing rule: if the 24-month market return is below 0 and 126-day market vol is high, cut momentum/breakout exposure and expect junk/loser rallies on market rebounds.

items.name: Low beta / betting-against-beta and low volatility
items.rules_or_formula: BAB: rank on estimated beta, shrunk toward the cross-sectional mean (0.6 weight on the time-series estimate). Long low-beta stocks levered to beta 1, short high-beta stocks de-levered to beta 1, rank-weighted. Low-vol: long the lowest-volatility or lowest-beta quintile.
items.evidence: BAB US 1926-2012: Sharpe 0.78. BBW 1968-2008: low-beta and low-vol portfolios earned annualized alphas of 2.6% and 2.1%. Critique (Novy-Marx-Velikov, 'Betting against betting against beta'): three nonstandard construction choices drive much of BAB's performance.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Exact BAB beta-estimation windows were not re-verified in this pass.
items.swing_engine_use: Mostly a sizing insight: high-beta names deliver less return per unit of risk, so penalize them in sizing.

items.name: Idiosyncratic volatility (IVOL) puzzle
items.rules_or_formula: IVOL = standard deviation of the residuals from regressing a stock's daily returns on the Fama-French 3 daily factors over the previous month. Sort into quintiles. High-IVOL stocks have low next-month returns.
items.data_needed: Daily returns plus FF daily factors (free, Ken French)
items.evidence: AHXZ 2009, 23 developed markets: the extreme IVOL quintile difference is -1.31%/mo after world market, size and value controls. HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): idiosyncratic, total and systematic volatility all fail replication (insignificant).
items.post_publication_and_costs: Driven by microcaps and EW weighting.
items.swing_engine_use: Avoid or penalize filter for very high-IVOL names, not an alpha source.

items.name: MAX / lottery effect
items.rules_or_formula: MAX = maximum daily return in the previous month (variants average the top-N daily returns). Sort into deciles. High-MAX stocks underperform the next month.
items.evidence: BCW: decile 10 minus 1 = -1.03%/mo (t=-2.83), all-stock breakpoints. HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): -0.34% (t=-1.14), -0.17% at 6 months and -0.07% at 12 months, all insignificant.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Fails VW replication.
items.swing_engine_use: Use as a lottery-stock flag: lower the conviction of setups whose prior month includes a huge single-day spike.

items.name: Amihud illiquidity
items.rules_or_formula: ILLIQ_i = (1/D) x sum over d of |R_(i,d)| / DollarVolume_(i,d), averaged over the prior ~12 months of trading days (often scaled by 10^6).
items.evidence: Amihud 2002: positive cross-sectional and time-series illiquidity premium (regressions that weight microcaps heavily). HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): high-minus-low 0.28% (t=1.31) at 1 month, 0.37% (t=1.73) at 6 months, 0.42% (t=1.99) at 12 months. The liquidity category overall fails replication, with 95 of 102 variables (93%) insignificant.
items.swing_engine_use: Cost and tradability gate (minimum liquidity, slippage model input), not alpha.

items.name: Gross and cash-based profitability
items.brand_or_source: Novy-Marx (JFE 2013); Ball et al. cash-based OP (as replicated by HXZ)
items.rules_or_formula: GP/A = (Revenue - COGS) / Total assets. Sort annually or monthly. Long the most profitable decile.
items.data_needed: Fundamentals from SEC XBRL companyfacts (Revenues, CostOfRevenue, Assets), free
items.evidence: Novy-Marx (1962-2010): top-minus-bottom 0.31%/mo, with about the predictive power of B/M. HXZ: Gpa 0.38% (t=2.62), but on lagged assets (Gla) only 0.16% (t=1.04), so the effect is confounded with investment. Cash-based operating profitability is a strong survivor at 0.63% (t=3.44, q-alpha 0.69, t=4.77).
items.swing_engine_use: Quality screen on swing candidates to avoid unprofitable junk during momentum crashes.

items.name: Quality minus junk (QMJ)
items.rules_or_formula: Quality score = average of z-scores for profitability, growth, safety and payout. Long the top 30%, short the bottom 30%, within large-cap and small-cap groups (Fama-French-style 2x3).
items.data_needed: Fundamentals (SEC XBRL), daily returns for the safety/beta components
items.evidence: Significant risk-adjusted returns in the US and across 24 countries. High-quality stocks are priced only modestly higher than junk.
items.post_publication_and_costs: The exact sub-component formulas were not re-verified here.
items.swing_engine_use: Secondary quality screen.

items.name: Post-earnings-announcement drift (SUE)
items.rules_or_formula: Time-series SUE = (EPS_q - EPS_(q-4)) / std of that seasonal change over the prior 8 quarters (minimum 6). Analyst SUE (Martineau) = (actual EPS - median of analysts' latest forecasts in the 90 days before) / price 5 days before. Each month sort on the latest SUE (fiscal quarter end within 6 months). Long the top decile. Bernard-Thomas used a 60-trading-day drift window.
items.data_needed: Quarterly EPS (SEC XBRL, free) plus announcement dates (8-K Item 2.02 / Alpha Vantage EARNINGS); analyst version needs consensus data
items.evidence: Bernard-Thomas: top-minus-bottom SUE spread positive in 41 of 48 quarters 1974-85. HXZ: Sue1 0.47% (t=3.42), but Sue6 0.19% and Sue12 0.11% are insignificant, and the q-alpha is 0.05. Martineau: since 2006 analyst SUE does not predict 60-day returns for all-but-microcap stocks, nor for microcaps since 2016; prices now react fully on day 0. Subrahmanyam (UCLA Anderson Review, Jan 2026): t falls from 2.18 to 1.43 once microcaps are excluded.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Effectively dead in large caps since 2006.
items.swing_engine_use: Do not hold for drift after an earnings beat in liquid names. Treat SUE as context only.

items.name: Earnings-announcement abnormal-return continuation (Abr)
items.rules_or_formula: Abr = sum over d=-2..+1 of (r_(i,d) - r_(m,d)) around the latest quarterly announcement (day 0), with the market return value-weighted. Each month sort on the most recent Abr (fiscal quarter end within 6 months, announcement after quarter end). Long the top decile, hold 1 month.
items.evidence: HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints, through 2014): Abr1 0.74%/mo (t=5.85), Abr6 0.30% (t=3.24), Abr12 0.22% (t=2.84). Announcement returns are among the anomalies the q-factor model leaves unexplained.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Post-2014 status is not verified. Martineau's post-2006 decay of SUE drift argues for re-testing on 2015-2026 data before relying on it.
items.swing_engine_use: Most relevant earnings item for swing: rank stocks by the market-adjusted 4-day reaction to the latest report. Re-test before use.

items.name: Earnings announcement premium
items.rules_or_formula: Each month: go long stocks expected to announce earnings that month (proxy: they announced in the same month a year or a quarter earlier) and underweight or short the others. The premium is largest for stocks with high past announcement-period volume.
items.evidence: FL: the buy-announcers strategy earns more than 60 bp/month, about 7%+ per year, strongly related to volume surges and imputed small-investor buying. It holds globally (Barber et al. 2013).
items.swing_engine_use: Calendar tilt: favor holding quality momentum names into scheduled reports. Gap risk is the cost.

items.name: Analyst forecast revision momentum
items.rules_or_formula: RE_t = sum over tau=1..6 of (f_(t-tau) - f_(t-tau-1)) / p_(t-tau-1), where f is the consensus mean FY1 EPS forecast and p the prior-month price; at least 4 monthly changes required. Variant dEf = (f_(t-1) - f_(t-2)) / (0.5|f_(t-1)| + 0.5|f_(t-2)|). Deciles; long the top.
items.data_needed: Monthly consensus EPS history (I/B/E/S, Zacks, FactSet), not in the free stack
items.evidence: CJL: price momentum and earnings momentum are not subsumed by each other, and the premium is highest when both point the same way. HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): Re1 0.81% (t=3.28), Re6 0.54% (t=2.49), dEf1 1.03%/mo.
items.swing_engine_use: Needs paid estimates data. Revision direction (if available) as a confirmation filter.

items.name: Revenue surprise
items.rules_or_formula: Rs = (revenue per share_q - revenue per share_(q-4)) / std of that change over the prior 8 quarters (minimum 6). Deciles monthly; long the top.
items.data_needed: Quarterly revenue and shares (SEC XBRL, free)
items.evidence: HXZ: Rs1 0.31%/mo, marginal (t of about 2.2).
items.swing_engine_use: Minor confirmation feature.

items.name: Opportunistic insider purchases
items.rules_or_formula: From SEC Form 4 (open-market purchases, code P; sales, code S): an insider is 'routine' if they traded in the same calendar month in each of the prior 3 years; all others are 'opportunistic'. Signal = opportunistic net buying in the prior month. Long those stocks, value-weighted, hold about 1 month.
items.data_needed: SEC EDGAR Form 4 XML (free) plus OHLCV
items.evidence: CMP (1986-2007): opportunistic trades earn 82 bp/mo value-weighted abnormal returns, routine trades about 0. Post-SOX (2-business-day Form 4 deadline): the 3-day CAR on purchase filings is 1.89% vs 0.59% pre-SOX. Prior sweep (Zhao 2026, microcaps): most of the edge is captured on the disclosure day.
items.post_publication_and_costs: The reaction is now fast. Enter at the open after the filing and expect a smaller drift.
items.swing_engine_use: Event feature: cluster or opportunistic buys by non-routine insiders upgrade a technical setup.

items.name: Short interest / days-to-cover
items.rules_or_formula: SR = short interest / shares outstanding. DTC = SR / average daily turnover (volume / shares outstanding). Sort monthly. High-DTC stocks underperform. APR: 'constrained' stocks have high SI and low institutional ownership.
items.data_needed: FINRA twice-monthly short interest (free), shares outstanding (SEC), daily volume
items.evidence: HLNSY: the DTC long-short earns about 1.2%/mo and beats SR as a predictor. APR (1988-2002): constrained stocks underperform 215 bp/mo equal-weighted but only an insignificant 39 bp value-weighted. Reg SHO pilot (easier shorting) cut anomaly long-short returns by 77 bp/mo, all from the short legs.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Strongest on the short/avoid side in small caps.
items.swing_engine_use: Avoid longs in the top DTC decile unless deliberately trading a squeeze. Use as a short-side screen.

items.name: Aggregate short interest index (market timing)
items.rules_or_formula: SII = equal-weighted cross-sectional average of short interest / shares outstanding, standardized to unit variance (detrending details not verified). High SII predicts low S&P 500 excess returns at 1-12 months.
items.data_needed: FINRA short interest for all stocks (free)
items.evidence: Out-of-sample 1990-2012 it beat the historical mean and 14 other predictors, with certainty-equivalent gains of 3.5-4.6%/yr (CXO summary).
items.swing_engine_use: Slow macro overlay only.

items.name: Same-calendar-month return seasonality
items.rules_or_formula: For the coming month m, score each stock by its average return in the same calendar month over prior years (lag 12, years 2-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16-20). Deciles; long the top; hold 1 month.
items.evidence: HS (NYSE/AMEX 1963-2002): annual-lag autocorrelation lasts up to 20 years and survives size, industry and factor controls. HXZ (VW, NYSE breakpoints): year-1 lag 0.65% (t=3.23), years 2-5 0.69% (t=4.0), 6-10 0.83% (t=4.91), 11-15 0.67% (t=4.66), 16-20 0.56% (t=3.29). It is one of the anomalies the q-factor model cannot explain.
items.swing_engine_use: Cheap tie-breaker feature for the monthly candidate rank. Needs 5+ years of history.

items.name: Gap-fill base rates (SPY)
items.rules_or_formula: Gap = open / prior close - 1, with |gap| < 0.1% treated as flat. An up-gap fills when the day's low reaches the prior close; a down-gap fills when the high reaches it. Statistics are bucketed by gap size, for same-day fills and fills within 5 sessions.
items.evidence: SPY up-gaps, same-day / 5-day fill rates (cases): 0.1-0.25% 78%/91% (1,209); 0.25-0.5% 60%/82% (1,337); 0.5-1% 46%/70% (928); 1-2% 26%/53% (290); 2%+ 27%/52% (67). Down-gaps: 80/92, 66/89, 43/76, 33/69, 29/60. Average open-to-close is about 0 for small gaps; +0.19% for 1-2% up-gaps and +0.49% for 2%+ down-gaps. These are descriptive base rates with no cost or significance tests.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Single-vendor statistics.
items.swing_engine_use: Prior for intraday entry placement: fade only small gaps. Gaps of 1% or more mostly do not fill same day, so do not assume 'gaps always fill'.

items.name: Overnight vs intraday return decomposition
items.rules_or_formula: r_overnight = Open_t / Close_(t-1) - 1. r_intraday = Close_t / Open_t - 1. Compute strategy or characteristic returns separately per leg; LPS rank on past overnight and intraday components.
items.data_needed: Daily OHLC (adjust opens for splits and dividends)
items.evidence: CCG (1993-2006): the US equity premium is earned overnight, not intraday. LPS (14 strategies): momentum and some reversal profits accrue entirely overnight; most other anomaly profits accrue intraday, with opposite signs in the other leg. Effects last years and are stronger in large-cap, high-price stocks. Explained by institutions trading intraday against momentum.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Rated C as a standalone daily close-to-open trade (costs too high); B as a feature.
items.swing_engine_use: Feature: momentum built mainly from overnight gains is the kind that persists. Time momentum entries near the close rather than the open.

items.name: Overnight drift (2-3 a.m. ET futures window)
items.rules_or_formula: S&P 500 futures returns concentrate in 02:00-03:00 ET, around the European open, and are linked to US closing order imbalances.
items.evidence: 1998-2019: about 3.6% annualized earned in that one hour. NY Fed 2026 follow-up: the window has averaged close to zero since 2021, as dispersion in closing order imbalances fell from 6.5% to 2.9%.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Disappeared after publication.
items.swing_engine_use: Not usable with daily data. Skip.

items.name: Turn-of-the-month (TOM)
items.rules_or_formula: Academic window: last trading day of the month through the 3rd trading day of the next month (days -1..+3). QS rule: buy the S&P 500 at the close of the 5th-to-last trading day, sell at the close of the 3rd trading day of the new month.
items.data_needed: Daily closes plus a trading calendar
items.evidence: McConnell-Xu (1926-2005): on average all of the US excess market return came at TOM. Since 1987: 0.14%/day VW at TOM vs -0.01% on the other days; found in 31 of 35 countries, not limited to small caps or year-ends. QS (S&P since 1960): CAGR 7% vs 7.5% buy-and-hold with about 33% time in market, max drawdown 27% vs 56%. Prior sweep: about 0.55% per 4-day window, 1986-2021.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Persistent but small. Turn-of-quarter has faded.
items.swing_engine_use: Calendar tilt: favor entries just before month-end and avoid exits during days -1..+3.

items.name: Pre-holiday effect
items.rules_or_formula: Hold the index on the trading day before an exchange holiday.
items.data_needed: Daily closes plus NYSE holiday calendar
items.evidence: LS (DJIA 1897-1986): pre-holiday days averaged 0.22% vs 0.0094% on other days. Ariel: gains concentrated late in the day. Extended to 1983-2019 (CFR, Ko 2021): only small firms still show it; large-firm differences are insignificant, especially after 1990.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Decayed in large caps.
items.swing_engine_use: Weak calendar tie-breaker only.

items.name: Pre-FOMC announcement drift
items.rules_or_formula: Hold the S&P 500 over the 24 hours before scheduled FOMC announcements (2 p.m. to 2 p.m.). The daily-data proxy is the close the day before to the announcement-day close, which includes the reaction.
items.data_needed: FOMC calendar (federalreserve.gov) plus daily or intraday index data
items.evidence: LM (1994-2011): +49 bp on average in the 24 hours before announcements, about 80% of annual realized excess returns. KWG (through Dec 2019): the drift essentially disappeared after 2015, with or without press conferences.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Gone after 2015.
items.swing_engine_use: Event-risk flag rather than a trade.

items.name: Day-of-week / weekend effect
items.rules_or_formula: Classic finding: Monday returns (Friday close to Monday close) are negative on average.
items.evidence: Schwert 2003: the weekend effect, together with size, value and dividend-yield effects, weakened or disappeared after publication as practitioners traded on it.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Disappeared.
items.swing_engine_use: Do not use.

items.name: Turnaround Tuesday
items.rules_or_formula: If Monday's close is at least 1% below Friday's close, buy SPY at Monday's close and sell at Tuesday's close.
items.evidence: SPY: 212 trades, average +0.3% per trade, 56% win rate, CAGR 1.8% at 2.5% market exposure. Practitioner backtest with no data-snooping correction.
items.swing_engine_use: Low-exposure overlay at most.

items.name: Internal Bar Strength (IBS) mean reversion
items.rules_or_formula: IBS = (Close - Low) / (High - Low). QS rule: buy at the close when IBS < 0.2, sell at the close when IBS > 0.8.
items.evidence: Pagonidis (ETFs from inception to 2013): significant next-day mean reversion for most equity index ETFs. Stronger in high-volatility and bear markets, after high-range or high-volume days, and early in the week. QS: works on SPY since 1993, but detailed statistics are paywalled. No cost or data-snooping-adjusted evidence was verified.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Index-ETF effect; weaker for single stocks.
items.swing_engine_use: Entry-timing helper on index or sector ETFs: prefer to buy pullbacks on low-IBS closes within an uptrend.

items.name: RSI(2) mean reversion
items.brand_or_source: Connors-Alvarez (2008); Backtrex out-of-sample tests (via prior sweep)
items.rules_or_formula: Long only when the close is above SMA(200). Buy when the 2-period Wilder RSI is below 5-10. Exit on a close above SMA(5) (or RSI above 65-70).
items.evidence: Backtrex (Oct 2016 - Oct 2026, S&P 500, 0.02% commission per side): CAGR 1.7% vs 13.5% buy-and-hold, 73 trades, 71.2% wins, profit factor 1.43, average win 1.22% vs average loss 2.10%. The original claims were in-sample (about 1995-2007).
items.post_publication_and_costs: Out-of-sample decay.
items.swing_engine_use: High win rate with negative skew and poor compounding. Use only as an entry-timing feature.

items.name: Survey: profitability of technical analysis
items.rules_or_formula: Meta-review of modern technical-trading studies.
items.evidence: Of 95 modern studies, 56 positive, 20 negative and 19 mixed. Most suffer from data snooping, ex-post selection of rules or search technologies, and weak risk and transaction-cost estimates. The prior sweep's '92 studies: 58/24/10' are the 2004 report figures.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Positive results cluster before about 1990.
items.swing_engine_use: Prior: assume any technical rule is snooped until tested with a multiple-testing correction.

items.name: Moving-average and trading-range-break rules (BLL) under White's Reality Check
items.rules_or_formula: BLL tested variable-length MA crossovers (short 1-5 days vs long 50-200 days, with 0 or 1% bands), fixed 10-day holds, and 50/150/200-day trading-range breakouts on the DJIA 1897-1986. STW built a 7,846-rule universe (filters, MAs, support/resistance, channel breakouts, OBV) and bootstrapped White's Reality Check over all of them.
items.evidence: STW: BLL's in-sample results survive the snooping adjustment, but the best rule is insignificant out of sample 1987-1996 (8.63%/yr before costs).
items.post_publication_and_costs: No net edge after 1986.
items.swing_engine_use: Do not use MA crossovers as standalone triggers.

items.name: False-discovery-rate test of technical rules
items.rules_or_formula: Apply FDR control across the STW rule universe on DJIA daily data 1897-2011, then test whether past top rules persist.
items.evidence: No persistence: an investor could not have picked the future best rules in advance. Even in-sample, performance is wiped out by low transaction costs.
items.swing_engine_use: Validation standard: apply FDR or Reality Check and costs to every rule we add.

items.name: Algorithmic chart patterns via kernel regression
items.rules_or_formula: Smooth prices with Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression (bandwidth 0.3 x the cross-validated optimum) over rolling 38-day windows (l=35 plus d=3 lag). Find local extrema. Head-and-shoulders = 5 extrema: max, min, higher max, min, max, with E1/E5 within 1.5% of their average and E2/E4 within 1.5%. Rectangles: tops and bottoms each within 0.75%. Double tops: within 1.5% and at least 22 days apart. 10 patterns in total (HS, IHS, broadening, triangle, rectangle and double tops/bottoms).
items.evidence: US stocks 1962-96: conditional return distributions after several patterns differ from unconditional ones, especially on Nasdaq ('incremental information'). Profits were not shown. Prior sweep: Osler (NY Fed) found HS trades unprofitable on average.
items.swing_engine_use: If patterns are used, use this objective detector (not eyeballing) and validate net returns.

items.name: Evidence-Based Technical Analysis rule tests
items.rules_or_formula: 6,402 binary long/short rules (trend, extreme-value, divergence) on the S&P 500 over 25 years (1980-2005), tested with White's Reality Check and Masters' Monte Carlo permutation.
items.data_needed: Daily index plus some non-price series
items.evidence: None of the 6,402 rules was statistically significant after data-mining-bias correction.
items.swing_engine_use: Methodology template: permutation tests and data-mining-bias correction.

items.name: Guru Grades (expert market-forecast accuracy)
items.rules_or_formula: Graded public S&P 500 directional forecasts against subsequent market moves.
items.evidence: 6,582 forecasts from 68 gurus (2005-2012): overall accuracy 46.9%, 47.4% averaged by guru, range 20-72%.
items.swing_engine_use: Ignore pundit market calls as inputs.

items.name: Bulkowski chart-pattern statistics
items.brand_or_source: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns / thepatternsite.com
items.rules_or_formula: Performance is measured from breakout to the subsequent high, and failure is a move of less than 5% after breakout. No stops, costs or significance tests. Example: high-and-tight flag (rises 90%+ in under 2 months, then a flag).
items.evidence: 30,000+ samples. High-and-tight flags rose about 22% after 1 month and 21% after 2 months. Cup-with-handle (fact-checked): rank 3 of 39, 5% failure, +54% average rise, 62% throwback, 61% hit the target. Failure rates doubled in 2003-07 vs the 1990s. The site itself (Sept 2021) says the statistics are outdated.
items.post_publication_and_costs: Ex-post 'ultimate high' measurement inflates results.
items.swing_engine_use: Descriptive priors only.

items.name: Kaufman Efficiency Ratio and adaptive MA (KAMA)
items.brand_or_source: Perry Kaufman, Trading Systems and Methods / Smarter Trading
items.rules_or_formula: ER = |C_t - C_(t-10)| / sum of |C_i - C_(i-1)| over 10 bars. SC = [ER x (2/3 - 2/31) + 2/31]^2. KAMA_t = KAMA_(t-1) + SC x (C_t - KAMA_(t-1)), seeded with an SMA. Defaults (10, 2, 30). High ER means a trending market; low ER means a noisy one, which favors mean reversion.
items.evidence: No independent peer-reviewed performance test was found in this pass. Kaufman's own book tests are not verified.
items.swing_engine_use: Cheap regime feature to route signals between trend and mean-reversion modules. Validate before trusting.

items.name: Post-publication decay haircut
items.rules_or_formula: For 97 published predictors, compare in-sample, out-of-sample pre-publication and post-publication returns.
items.evidence: Returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication, so about 32 points come from publication-informed trading. Bigger declines hit predictors with high in-sample returns. Returns remain higher in high-idiosyncratic-risk, illiquid stocks.
items.swing_engine_use: Planning haircut: assume live edge is at most about half of the published edge.

items.name: Replicating anomalies (microcap control)
items.rules_or_formula: Re-test 447-452 anomalies with NYSE breakpoints and value-weighted returns.
items.evidence: 64-65% are insignificant at 5% and 85% fail at t>=3. 95 of 102 liquidity/friction variables fail, including short-term reversal, IVOL, MAX and Amihud. Momentum, earnings-announcement returns, revisions, residual momentum, industry momentum, seasonality and cash profitability survive.
items.swing_engine_use: Always backtest VW, or exclude stocks below the NYSE 20th size percentile.

items.name: Trading-cost taxonomy of anomalies
items.rules_or_formula: Effective-spread costs for 23 anomalies, plus cost mitigation (buy/hold spread, staggered rebalancing).
items.evidence: Most anomalies with under 50% monthly one-sided turnover keep significant net spreads when designed to cut costs; few with higher turnover do. A buy/hold spread is the most effective mitigation.
items.swing_engine_use: Engine rule: enter only in the top 10% of a rank, exit only below the top 20-30%.

items.name: Replication-crisis rebuttal and open-source factor data
items.rules_or_formula: Bayesian replication of about 150 factors in 93 countries; open-source code and data for 300+ predictors.
items.evidence: JKP: most factors replicate, cluster into 13 themes and work out of sample internationally. CZ: 98% of the 161 clearly significant predictors reproduce with t>1.96; slope 0.90 on original t-stats, R^2 83%. Free monthly long-short returns are downloadable.
items.swing_engine_use: Free benchmark: download CZ portfolio returns to sanity-check our signal implementations.
